A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProLIP research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, figures and tables support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, retrieval, hierarchy, prompt-reweighting and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and C.1–C.5.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds fine-tuning, efficiency, data-filtering and image-manipulation experiments.

M1.justification: The Gaussian representation, uncertainty token, PPCL, inclusion and VIB objectives, and BPRW updates remain unchanged (Equations 1–6 and Algorithm 1). Additional fine-tuning and traversal descriptions do not establish a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: The existing training corpora, 38-task evaluation suite, HierarCaps and HierarImgs are retained. Appendix C.8 adds DataComp small-track dataset filtering and ImageNet center-occlusion and PGD scenarios. MNIST and ImageNet, used in new uncertainty analyses, were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Table C.7 introduces comparisons against unfiltered and random subsets, LAION-2B filtering, language/size heuristics, and CLIP-based filtering. Table C.6 adds explicit efficiency comparisons against multi-head and deterministic architectures. AdamP ProLIP rows disappear from Tables C.1–C.2, although Appendix B.1 retains their discussion; the main CLIP and SigLIP comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds fine-tuned ViT-B/16, SO400M/14 and DFN-initialized ViT-H/14 configurations; ViT-L/16 fine-tuning already appeared in v1. New protocols include timing inference on 50,000 images, measuring hierarchy-order consistency, testing 0–10% center occlusion, and applying 1/5/10/40 PGD iterations to 1,000 images. Table C.5 also adds the epsilon=-100, c=10 setting.

E4.justification: New analyses examine architecture overhead (Table C.6), agreement with existing human-validated caption hierarchies (Appendix C.6), uncertainty–accuracy relationships, and responses to occlusion and adversarial manipulation (Appendix C.8). Figure B.1 adds comparative traversal cases, and Table C.5 extends sensitivity testing. The original loss ablations in Tables C.3–C.4 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added analyses of predicted uncertainty do not introduce experimental error bars or estimates of variability across runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds fine-tuning scores, inference timings, 90.0% adjacent hierarchy-order agreement, and filtering and robustness outcomes. It revises numerous per-task entries in Table C.1 and removes detailed AdamP results. Table 1's 67.8% ImageNet and 57.9% average row already appeared under epsilon=-10, c=10 in v1 Table C.5, so it is not a newly demonstrated same-setting gain. Tables 2–3 and the 74.6%/75.8% headline results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds a derivation relating equal-weight Gaussian-mixture CSD to concatenated Gaussian representations, and Appendix A.6 adds a counterexample argument involving KL minus reverse KL. These supplement the retained PPCL and inclusion derivations and BPRW equations; the core mathematical formulation is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: large-scale probabilistic pretraining, efficient uncertainty tokens, inclusion loss, and uncertainty-based downstream applications. The headline accuracy claims are unchanged; new appendix evidence primarily supports existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially expands the distinction between unimodal and cross-modal uncertainty and its dependence on training captions. Appendix C.8 distinguishes ProLIP uncertainty from classification uncertainty and interprets opposite MNIST/ImageNet correlations. Appendix D adds substantive discussion of diagonal covariance, mixture models and distribution-dependent closed forms, while B.2 explains fine-tuning performance tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 adds pretrained-weight access information and a reproducibility statement. Appendix B.2 documents checkpoint sources, pooling conversion, 224×224 resolution, learning rate 5e-5, zero weight decay and the fine-tuning budget. The existing VIB loss and traversal procedure receive fuller documentation. Appendix B.1 changes the recommended epsilon from -10 to -100 at c=10; its stated default remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting scaling, DFN initialization, adversarial testing and ImageNet label ambiguity, including Cherti, Fang, Madry, Beyer and Yun. Section 4.4 changes attribution of the traversal protocol from Desai et al. to Alper and Averbuch-Elor. The central positioning against deterministic and earlier probabilistic VLMs remains intact.

P1.justification: Although the main text receives mostly light edits, the appendix exposition is substantially expanded and reorganized. A conceptual introduction now precedes the derivations, ablations receive a separate subsection, the BPRW discussion is reordered, and dedicated reproducibility and limitations sections are added. References move from before the appendices to the document's end.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures A.1, A.2, B.1 and C.4 and Tables C.6–C.9, expands Tables 1 and C.1, and redesigns Table C.2 around fine-tuned backbones and FLOPs. Existing figures are resized or relocated; v1's BPRW histogram Figure C.4 survives as v2 Figure C.6 rather than being removed.

improvement.justification: The added efficiency measurements, uncertainty checks and fine-tuning details improve empirical support and reproducibility beyond v1, while revised Table C.1 entries improve consistency with summary results. These gains are tempered by a new mathematical inconsistency: Appendix A.6 treats negative raw inclusion scores as validating both directions of the inclusion test, although Equation 4 defines an antisymmetric difference. The revision therefore offers a useful but qualified net improvement.
